claims.statement: HO 04 35 is an attachment-dependent endorsement whose provisions control conflicting policy provisions while nonconflicting policy terms remain applicable; the supplied 2014-04 edition is superseded by 2023-02 for policies effective on or after 2023-02-01, while the older edition remains applicable to policies written under it, and both source files identify the endorsement line as HO-6.

HO 04 35 (2014-04) covers an insured's allocated assessment from an authorized association when it results from covered direct physical loss to association property or from a liability claim against the association, and it can cover an association deductible arising from a covered loss when the association's property insurance applies.

HO 04 35 (2023-02) covers an assessment legally charged to an owner or tenant for covered direct physical loss to Collective Property, an Association Master Policy deductible tied to covered loss, or Property Damage for which the association is legally liable and that results from a covered occurrence.

The maximum Loss Assessment Coverage limit is $10,000 under HO 04 35 (2014-04) and $25,000 under HO 04 35 (2023-02); payments do not increase the applicable limit, and the limit is not increased by multiple insureds, claims, assessments, or associations.

Neither HO 04 35 edition states a numeric deductible: 2014-04 applies the applicable policy deductible to a covered assessment and once to the same covered loss or liability claim, while 2023-02 applies the applicable deductible only to the covered assessment amount before payment and does not apply it to uncovered charges.

Both editions require a valid, enforceable, properly allocated assessment and prompt notice with supporting records; the 2023-02 edition additionally requires notice of changes such as revision, withdrawal, reduction, increase, or reallocation.

HO 04 35 payment is limited to the insured's covered allocated share and is reduced by duplicate or legally available recovery; both editions preserve duties to cooperate, protect property, preserve evidence, and avoid unauthorized voluntary payments or settlements.

The editions exclude assessment charges for ordinary maintenance or improvement, wear or deterioration, defective design or workmanship, intentional or criminal conduct, fines or penalties, contractual-only obligations, and excluded causes of loss; they also preserve applicable policy exclusions unless the endorsement expressly provides otherwise.

HO-6 2014-04 Section I Additional Coverages provides $1,000 for a loss assessment arising from covered loss to property owned collectively by association members and separately provides up to $500 of approved defense costs for a covered assessment claim; its separate Section II contains assessment coverage for covered claims or direct physical loss, with its own exclusions including an association deductible or retained amount. Attaching HO 04 35 (2014-04) controls conflicting provisions and provides a $10,000 Loss Assessment Coverage limit for its stated scope.

HO-6 2023-02 Section I Additional Coverages provides $2,000 for a loss assessment arising from covered loss to collectively owned property and separately covers an association deductible assessed for covered damage when allocated under the governing documents; Section II separately addresses a loss assessment arising from covered property damage for which an insured is liable. HO 04 35 (2023-02) provides a $25,000 maximum for its assessment coverage when attached.

HO 04 35 assessment coverage is distinct from ordinary Section II Coverage E: Coverage E pays an insured's legally owed bodily-injury or property-damage damages and provides a defense for a covered suit, while HO 04 35 pays an association assessment; the 2023-02 endorsement may defend an action brought against the insured concerning an assessment but does not create a duty to defend the Association itself.

The supplied HO-3 2024-03 base form's Section I Additional Coverages provides $2,000 for an assessment arising from direct physical loss to collectively owned corporation or association property caused by a covered cause of loss; the applicable Section I deductible applies to covered loss unless modified by endorsement. Its separate Coverage E pays legally owed bodily-injury or property-damage damages and provides a defense for a covered claim or suit, but is not itself the Section I assessment grant.

The supplied state amendatory forms are separate HO-3 documents and use state-specific assessment labels or documentation rules without stating a standalone HO 04 35 dollar limit: Florida refers to a loss assessment additional coverage limit, California, Texas, Illinois, and North Carolina refer to a special assessment limit, and Louisiana and Colorado refer to an association assessment limit.
The customer FAQ instructs staff not to assume an association assessment is covered and to identify why it was issued and what property or loss it concerns before discussing payment.

A condominium master-policy gap requires separate review of association responsibility, unit-owner property, covered cause or liability, and the owner's legally allocated assessment obligation because the declaration, master policy, and unit-owner policy may assign different responsibility for the same loss; an assessment notice or master-policy response does not itself establish unit-owner coverage.

Training and other guidance may organize fact gathering and identify coverage questions, but cannot add, remove, or revise coverage; the applicable policy and attached endorsement language controls the coverage position and assessment limit.

Under HO 04 35 (2023-02), an association Master Policy deductible can be a covered assessment component only when the Association charges it to the insured for covered Direct Physical Loss to Collective Property, while the applicable policy deductible is separately applied to the covered Loss Assessment amount before payment.
